message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I did the right thing by telling my sister that the world doesn't revolve around her. Let me start by understanding the situation better. My sister is 19, and she's a lot younger than me. From what I remember, she was spoiled growing up because our parents could afford things like vacations and other activities that I wasn't able to do when I was a kid. Now, she's controlling and gets mad over really small things, like peeing a bit on the toilet seat, forgetting to fill the Brita water filter, or leaving a single pot out at night. She calls these things 'disrespectful,' but I don't get why they bother her so much. I mean, stuff happens, right? I think she needs to let things go more. Yesterday, she was making dinner for herself, my mom, and dad. I went to put something in the oven, and she said, "I needed that for anything." I told her we could split the oven or she could wait 20 minutes. She got mad, and I got fed up with her attitude. I told her the world doesn't revolve around her. She scoffed and said the same back to me. I told her her attitude was going to get her into trouble in the real world, and she said she'd be fine, thanks for the advice. I'm wondering if I overreacted. Did I do the right thing? I don't know why she hates me so much and is so controlling. Maybe it's because she's younger and still figuring things out, but I feel like I'm the one who's been through more and should be the mature one here. On one hand, I think it's important to stand up for yourself and not let someone's controlling behavior affect you. Telling her the world doesn't revolve around her was a way to assert my boundaries. But on the other hand, maybe I should have handled it more calmly or tried to understand her perspective better. I also wonder if her behavior is a reflection of her own insecurities or if she's just going through a phase. Maybe she feels neglected or overlooked because I was the one who had to grow up without the same privileges. That could be why she's acting out now. I should consider how my approach might have made things worse. By telling her off, did I escalate the situation? Or did I just need to set some boundaries to protect myself from her constant criticism and control? I also think about how our parents might view this. They might have spoiled her, and now she's struggling to adjust to reality. Maybe I should talk to them about it, but I don't want to involve them if it can be resolved between us. In the end, I want to maintain a good relationship with her, but I also don't want to be walked all over. Finding that balance is tricky. I need to communicate my feelings without being confrontational, but I also need to make sure she understands that her behavior isn't acceptable. So, did I do the right thing? I'm not sure. It felt necessary at the time, but maybe there's a better way to handle it in the future.
